sentences.text: Revenue grew from $26.6 billion in FY2016 to $45.7 billion in FY2025, a 6.2% CAGR [F1][F10][F157].
The path was cyclical: revenue peaked at $61.3 billion in FY2023, then fell 15.6% in FY2024 and 11.7% in FY2025 [F8][D367][D412].
FY2024's decline reflected lower shipment volumes, as rising grain stocks, lower commodity prices and elevated interest rates weighed on agriculture demand [P17][D367].
The FY2021 step up of 23.9% came from higher shipment volumes, sales mix and price realization [P43][P42][D231].
Production and Precision Agriculture was the largest driver, adding 9.5pp to FY2023 growth at a 44.6% revenue share [D863][D861].
In FY2025 it fell 17.0%, cut 7.0pp from growth and left a 38.9% revenue share [D868][D869][D867].
The filing ties this to a 30% volume drop in the U.S. and Canada, partly offset by a 22% rise in Brazil [P10][D868].
In FY2024 operating income fell 30.2% on a 15.6% revenue decline, an incremental margin of 41.1% [D368][D367][D388].
Diluted EPS compounded at 16.1% against 14.2% for net income as diluted shares fell from 316.6 million to 271.7 million [F162][F160][X110][X119].
FY2024 operating margin of 17.5% was above the 12.1% window median, below the 21.2% high and above the 9.7% low [F30][D1335][D1334][D1333].
FY2025 operating income is not in the pack, so the operating margin story ends at FY2024.
The FY2024 margin fell 3.7pp, with SG&A costing 1.9pp, R&D 0.9pp and other lines 0.9pp [D378][D391][D390][D392].
The filing cites lower volumes and production inefficiencies raising manufacturing overhead, partly offset by lower material and profit-sharing costs [P16][D392].
The largest move was FY2021's 6.1pp gain, with SG&A adding 2.1pp and R&D 1.0pp as price realization and absent 2020 separation charges cut costs [D243][D256][D255][P45].
FY2025 operating cash flow was 1.48x net income and free cash flow 1.21x, above the 0.91x window median [D401][D402][D1347].
Operating cash flow of $7.46 billion came from earnings adjusted for non-cash provisions and lower receivables, partly offset by an OPEB contribution [P5][F80].
Free cash flow margin of 13.4% beat the 11.6% median, while capex was 3.0% of revenue and 0.61x D&A [D398][D1341][D397][D403].
Net cash was -$5.52 billion in FY2025, an improvement from -$6.21 billion in FY2024 [D407][D362].
Net cash was -12.1% of revenue against a -38.8% peer median, the 100th percentile among seven industrials peers [D408][D1358][D1357].
Buybacks plus dividends fell to $2.86 billion, 46.9% of free cash flow, from $8.64 billion and 121.9% in FY2023 [D409][D410][D319][D320].
Diluted shares fell 1.9% in FY2025 after a 5.6% drop in FY2024 [D427][D384].
R1, high: revenue fell 15.6% in FY2024 and 11.7% in FY2025, leaving FY2025 25.4% below FY2023 [D367][D412][F10][F8].
R2 to R7 overlap: Production and Precision Agriculture, 38.9% of revenue, fell 17.0% while its segment margin dropped from 25.6% in FY2023 to 15.0% [D867][D868][D1307][D1309].
Construction and Forestry, 25.5% of revenue, fell 11.8% and its segment margin fell from 18.0% to 8.8%; the cited filings do not explain it [D889][D890][D1317][D1319].
Provision for credit losses was $296 million in FY2025 against -$16 million in FY2023, and the allowance rose on elevated agriculture and turf delinquencies [X171][X169][P4].
Production and Precision Agriculture segment margin above 15.0% in the FY2026 10-K would suggest a trough; below it would extend the fall from 25.6% in FY2023 [D1309][D1307].

Free cash flow to net income below the 0.91x window median, against 1.21x now, in the FY2026 10-K would confirm normalising conversion, as the filing forecasts lower 2026 equipment operating cash flow [D1347][D402][P6].
Provision for credit losses above the FY2025 level of $296 million in the FY2026 10-K would confirm rising credit stress in agriculture and turf accounts [X171][P4].
